page2_img_1.png.title: Agent notes UI showing diff reasoning, references, next steps, and human guidance
page2_img_1.png.description: A screenshot of the prototype’s “Agent Notes” panel that presents the agent’s current reasoning about a differential test: it states the diff is an ErrorCode change (specific codes redacted) and tentatively attributes it to a deprecation/rollout observed in historical comments. Below the reasoning are two blue chips showing UUIDs (5325ecd2-... and 6b2fe749-...) that link the agent’s claims to specific artifacts for traceability. A green “Next Steps” box lists actionable checks (e.g., call 'lookup_error' and review test/production logs) and suggests labeling the diff as 'NewFeature' if rollout patterns match; beneath that is a “Human Guidance” area with an 11s timer and a user message asking the agent to search team messages for related discussion. The view demonstrates how the agent documents belief updates, cites concrete artifact IDs, and solicits synchronous human input to steer the investigation.

page3_img_1.png.title: Evolving human–AI knowledge network linking system and tacit data
page3_img_1.png.description: A schematic vision of a unified knowledge space where system data (code, commits, requirements, logs) and human data (wiki pages, messages, meeting transcripts, business goals) feed into a central paired representation labeled “Code Graph” and “Natural Language Graph” (accessed via GraphRAG). Agents and tools — including a traceability tool, GraphRAG tool calls, and multi-agent “Competing Hypotheses Agents” — read from and write evidence and notes to the graph; arrows marked Input/Output/Update show how information flows between components and to a human reviewer, and dotted versus solid lines denote synchronous versus asynchronous interactions. Historical info, process references, and agent traces are collected on the right and consumed by an ML process that produces “Process Insights,” which in turn update relationships and “Evolve Processes,” closing the loop so the network and workflows can be refined over time. Black nodes with thin outlines indicate the initial prototype elements while blue, thicker nodes indicate planned next-phase components (dynamic relationships and process analysis).
